strategy_title: Enable TF32 in Triton dot to improve IPC
strategy_description: Changing ALLOW_TF32 from False to True in Triton tl.dot calls reduces warp cycles per issued instruction (2.61→2.45) and increases issue slot utilization (37.5%→41.2%), yielding a modest but real latency reduction. The change allows the dot product to use Tensor Core MMA instructions instead of FP32 FFMA, which completes faster per cycle even when the kernel is severely underutilized due to a small grid. This optimization is most effective when the kernel already has a compute bottleneck or high stall-due-to-no-eligible-warp fraction.
slow_pseudocode:
# Triton kernel constexpr
ALLOW_TF32: tl.constexpr = False
...
acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=ALLOW_TF32)  # uses FP32 FFMA
fast_pseudocode:
# Triton kernel constexpr
ALLOW_TF32: tl.constexpr = True
...
acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=ALLOW_TF32)  # uses TF32 Tensor Core MMA
applicable_when: Triton kernel uses tl.dot with ALLOW_TF32=False; IssueSlotUtilization rule fires with high 'No Eligible' warp percentage (>50%); kernel is compute-bound or has significant dot-product work in inner loop; FP32 precision in matrix multiply is not strictly required (attention scores, general GEMM)
do_not_apply_when: Full FP32 mantissa precision is required (e.g., scientific computing, loss accumulation); kernel is purely memory-bound with negligible dot-product work; the speedup from TF32 is already captured by using fp16/bf16 inputs to tl.dot
framework_notes: Triton-specific: set ALLOW_TF32: tl.constexpr = True and pass allow_tf32=ALLOW_TF32 to tl.dot. In CUDA, the equivalent is setting cublasMath_t to CUBLAS_TF32_TENSOR_OP_MATH or using __nv_bfloat16 accumulation. Note: the planned grid fix (1→32768) did not appear in the actual diff, suggesting only the TF32 change was applied; the 5.5% speedup is attributable solely to TF32 enabling improved IPC on the existing single-block kernel.

strategy_title: Enable TF32 and Fix Grid for Batched Matmul
strategy_description: When a Triton batched matmul kernel launches with grid=(1,1,1) but the batch dimension is large (e.g. 32768), only one batch slice is computed and waves_per_SM stays at 0.0. Correcting the grid to (grid_m*grid_n, batch_size, 1) ensures all batch slices are covered. Simultaneously enabling allow_tf32=True in tl.dot routes computation through Tensor Cores instead of FP32 FFMA, improving IPC active from 1.50 to 1.59 and reducing elapsed cycles from 9022 to 8810. The combined effect yields a modest ~5% speedup; the grid fix is a correctness requirement while TF32 provides the compute efficiency gain.
slow_pseudocode:
# Triton kernel
ALLOW_TF32: tl.constexpr = False
...
acc = tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=ALLOW_TF32)

# Launch
grid = (1, 1, 1)  # BUG: only 1 of 32768 batch slices computed
kernel[grid](...)
fast_pseudocode:
# Triton kernel
ALLOW_TF32: tl.constexpr = True
...
acc = tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=ALLOW_TF32)

# Launch
batch_size = arg_0.shape[0]  # e.g. 32768
grid_m = triton.cdiv(M, BLOCK_M)
grid_n = triton.cdiv(N, BLOCK_N)
grid = (grid_m * grid_n, batch_size, 1)
kernel[grid](...)
applicable_when: Triton batched matmul kernel with grid_size=1 and waves_per_SM=0.0 despite large batch dimension; ALLOW_TF32=False constexpr in kernel body; K is small (<=128) making TF32 rounding error negligible; NCU LaunchConfiguration rule fires with high speedup_pct (>90%)
do_not_apply_when: Grid is already correctly sized to cover all batch slices; K is large (>512) where TF32 mantissa truncation may accumulate significant error; output requires strict FP32 precision (atol < 1e-3); kernel is not a batched matmul pattern
framework_notes: Triton-specific: ALLOW_TF32 is a tl.constexpr that gates the allow_tf32 argument to tl.dot. In CUDA, the equivalent is using CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F_FAST_TF32 or setting cudaDeviceSetSharedMemConfig. The grid fix is framework-agnostic: any batched kernel must have grid dim covering all batch elements.

strategy_title: Enable TF32 Tensor Cores in Triton tl.dot
strategy_description: When a Triton kernel uses tl.dot with ALLOW_TF32=False, it falls back to FP32 FFMA instead of TF32 Tensor Cores, leaving significant throughput on the table. Setting ALLOW_TF32=True (as a tl.constexpr) routes the dot product through Tensor Core MMA instructions, which deliver ~8x higher throughput on H100/A100-class GPUs. The improvement is modest here (1.04x) because the kernel is severely underutilized (grid=1 block, 0 waves across 132 SMs), so the TF32 benefit is masked by the launch bottleneck; the L2 hit rate improved from 65.8% to 75.4% and elapsed cycles dropped from 9022 to 8844.
slow_pseudocode:
# Triton kernel
ALLOW_TF32: tl.constexpr = False
...
acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=ALLOW_TF32)  # uses FP32 FFMA
fast_pseudocode:
# Triton kernel
ALLOW_TF32: tl.constexpr = True
...
acc += tl.dot(a, b, allow_tf32=ALLOW_TF32)  # uses TF32 Tensor Cores
applicable_when: Triton kernel uses tl.dot with ALLOW_TF32=False or unset; FMA pipeline is the highest-utilized pipe (>20% active cycles); kernel is compute-bound or has moderate occupancy; FP32 precision is not strictly required (TF32 truncates mantissa from 23 to 10 bits); BLOCK_K >= 16 so Tensor Core MMA tiles are well-utilized
do_not_apply_when: Strict FP32 numerical precision is required (e.g., scientific computing with large accumulation chains); BLOCK_K is very small (<16) making MMA tiles inefficient; kernel is already memory-bandwidth bound (DRAM throughput >80%) where compute throughput is not the bottleneck; the kernel grid is severely under-launched (grid=1 with 100+ SMs) without fixing the launch configuration first, as the TF32 benefit will be masked
framework_notes: Triton-specific: set ALLOW_TF32: tl.constexpr = True in the kernel signature or pass ALLOW_TF32=True as a constexpr at the call site. The tl.dot call must use allow_tf32=ALLOW_TF32. Keep ACC_TYPE=tl.float32 so accumulation remains FP32 even with TF32 inputs. In CUDA, the equivalent is using __nv_bfloat16 or setting cudaDeviceSetSharedMemConfig; in cuBLAS it is CUBLAS_COMPUTE_32F_FAST_TF32.
